requirement:
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`. Every obligation has code that carries it out and a test that asserts the outcome.

**Location and separate record per run**
- `src/authoring/usage.rs#impl[UsageLog]/fn[start]` creates `<state>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json`, using the state root from `usage_state_root` in `src/authoring/mod.rs` (`config::state_root`).
- Each run gets its own run id and file.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[usage_record_identifies_its_run_and_unusable_state_is_reported]` checks the directory, that the file is named after `run_id`, and that exactly one file exists.

**Identifying fields**
- `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageRecord]` holds `version`, `run_id`, `project_root`, `subject`, `subject_kind`, `backend`, `model`, `start_time_ms`, `end_time_ms`, `outcome`, `determination`, `evidence_output` and `evidence_written`.
- These fields are set in `UsageLog::start`, `author_evidence_with_options`, `prepare_assessment`, `configured_record`, `assess` and `assess_subject`.
- Backend and model are set once the configuration is known. They are `None` otherwise, which matches "when known".
- The record keeps the determination kind only (`judgment.kind()`), not FIXME entries.
- The same CLI test asserts version, `project_root`, subject, `subject_kind`, backend, model, `evidence_output` and the start/end times.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[usage_record_of_an_early_failure_identifies_its_subject_kind]` covers a run that fails early.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]` check determination kinds `true`, `false` and `FIXME`. They also check that `determination` is null when nothing was accepted.

**`evidence_output` and `evidence_written`**
- `author_evidence_with_options` sets `evidence_output` to `file` or `stdout`.
- `configured_assessment` sets `evidence_written = true` after either the file write or the stdout write succeeds. `PendingAssessment::persisted` does the same for batch file writes.
- The stdout test asserts `evidence_output == "stdout"` and `evidence_written == true`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[failed_evidence_write_keeps_the_accepted_judgment_in_usage]` asserts a failed write leaves `evidence_written` false while the determination is kept.

**Usage stays outside the project in stdout mode**
- `usage_state_root` refuses a state root inside the project before creating it, in both modes.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[usage_state_inside_the_project_is_refused_before_creating_it]` runs both file and `--stdout` modes and checks the directory is not created.
- An unusable state location is reported and no evidence is written (CLI test, blocker file and missing `HOME` cases).

**No FIXME entry text, source, prompts, responses or rationale**
- The record has no fields for them.
- `src/authoring/usage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[input_metadata_counts_components_and_reads_without_persisting_source]` and the CLI test `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` assert that secrets, the rationale and `#125` are absent from the serialized record.
- `src/authoring/usage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_outcomes_are_distinct_and_unknown_names_do_not_leak_model_text]` checks that unknown tool names do not leak model text.

**Failed, cancelled and unfinished runs are distinguishable**
- A new record starts with outcome `unfinished` and a null `end_time_ms`.
- `UsageLog::finish`, `PendingAssessment::failed` and `prepare_assessment` set `cancelled` for `Interrupted` errors and `failed` otherwise. Success is `completed`.
- `src/authoring/usage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cancelled_request_persists_elapsed_time_and_incomplete_totals]` checks the unfinished and cancelled outcomes.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure]` checks the failed outcome.
- The submission-failure CLI test and the early-failure test also check failed runs.

**Persistence**
- `UsageLog::save` writes the file to disk and `finish` rewrites it. A failure to record usage is reported, and the error text states whether evidence was written.

The extra fields (requests, inputs, tokens, policy) are specified by `usage_requests`, `usage_inputs` and `policy`, which the same code marks.

:::{req} state_location
Habeas MUST store persistent per-user activity state under
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/habeas` on Unix when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute, nonempty path,
otherwise under `$HOME/.local/state/habeas`. On Windows it MUST use
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/habeas/state`. `HOME` and `LOCALAPPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. Features MUST use a named subdirectory under that
state root and document their record formats and locations.
State MUST persist across invocations and MUST NOT be stored in the project
repository, the configuration file, or a disposable cache directory. Habeas MUST
create the required directories when recording state. If it cannot determine or
write the state location, the operation requiring that state MUST report the
failure and MUST NOT claim that its history was recorded.
